codes.rationale: The discharge summary documents LLL community-acquired pneumonia with no organism identified. It was present on admission and treated throughout the stay. Respiratory failure was also present on admission, so either could be sequenced first under OCG II.C. I chose pneumonia as the underlying cause.
codes.critic_reason: LLL CAP documented consistently by ED, H&P, pulmonology, and discharge summary, with radiographic support. No organism was identified. Per OCG I.C.10.b, when respiratory failure is present on admission with pneumonia, the respiratory failure may be sequenced first, but pneumonia as the underlying cause is also acceptable.

codes.rationale: Acute hypoxic respiratory failure is documented by pulmonology and the attending. It is clinically supported by SpO2 84% on room air, accessory muscle use, and P/F ratio of about 150. It was present at ED presentation.

Clinical indicators are SpO2 84% RA, pO2 54 on 4L, P/F about 150, RR 30-32, and accessory muscle use, with HFNC treatment. It was POA. issues.summary: Pneumonia and acute respiratory failure were both present on admission and both meet the principal diagnosis definition. Sequencing is a judgment call, and J96.01 as principal would be defensible.

The CXR report notes emphysematous changes not well evaluated on portable technique, while pulmonology documents no clinical evidence of obstructive lung disease. This is not a diagnosis and should not be coded, but note it so no emphysema code is added without provider documentation.
